7 signs your website is costing you leads (and how to fix each one)

A website rarely breaks loudly. It just stops sending enquiries, one slow page and one lost form at a time. Here are the seven signs I look for first on a small business site, how to check each one yourself, and what the fix involves.

Genesis MontillaPublished November 12, 2026

// key_takeaways

  • Most lost leads come from small, fixable things: slow mobile pages, a buried call to action, forms nobody tested and no tracking.
  • You can check all seven signs yourself in about 15 minutes with a phone and a test enquiry.
  • Fix them in order: forms first, then tracking, then calls to action, speed and content.

Why websites lose leads quietly#

A broken website is easy to spot. A website that works but leaks enquiries isn't. The page loads, the photos look fine and the phone still rings now and then, so nobody digs in. Meanwhile visitors leave because a page was slow, a button was hard to find or a form went nowhere.

These are the seven signs I check first when a business asks me why their site isn't bringing in work. Keep count of the ones you recognise. There's a checklist further down that adds them up.

1. It's slow on a phone#

Most of your visitors are on a phone, often on mobile data. If the first screen takes several seconds to show anything useful, many of them go back to the search results and tap the next business.

Check it: open your site on your phone with Wi-Fi off, then run it through PageSpeed Insights and look at the mobile score. The fix: resize and compress images, remove plugins and scripts you don't use, and load fonts and tracking tags with care.

2. The next step is hard to find#

Visitors decide fast. If they have to hunt for how to contact you, book or buy, they won't. Every page should make the next step obvious: one clear button, the same wording everywhere, visible on a phone without scrolling.

Check it: ask someone who has never seen your site to book a call or request a quote on their phone, and watch without helping. The fix: one main call to action per page, repeated in the header and at natural stopping points.

3. Forms that never arrive#

This is the most expensive sign, because the visitor did everything right. Contact forms fail silently all the time: emails land in spam, a plugin update breaks sending, or the connection to your CRM or booking tool was never finished.

Check it: submit your own contact form today, and every booking or quote form you have. Did each one arrive, and where? The fix: reliable email sending through SMTP, a clear confirmation message for the visitor, and a test after every plugin or theme update.

// from real work

For Simple Forwarding, I worked in a Hostinger staging environment to review and improve the site before changes went live: fixing links, refining Calendly calls to action and improving mobile navigation. Small things, but each one sat between a visitor and a booking.

4. You can't tell where leads come from#

If you don't know which pages, ads or searches bring enquiries, you can't do more of what works. Many small business sites have Google Analytics installed but no conversion tracking, so form submissions, calls and bookings never show up as results.

Check it: in Google Analytics, can you see how many forms, calls or bookings came in last month, and from where? The fix: Google Tag Manager with an event for each kind of lead, marked as key events in GA4, plus Meta Pixel or Google Ads conversions if you run ads.

5. It breaks at some screen sizes#

Sites usually get approved on a laptop. Then a menu overlaps the logo on a tablet, a table pushes the page sideways on a phone, or the main button drops out of view. Visitors read that as careless, and careless isn't who they want to hire.

Check it: open your main pages on a phone, a tablet and a laptop, and turn the phone sideways. The fix: responsive layout fixes in your page builder or theme, then a check at several screen widths before every launch.

6. Google can't tell what each page is about#

If every page has the same title, there's no clear main heading, and all your services live on one long page, search engines and AI tools have little to work with. You show up for your business name, and not much else.

Check it: search site:yourdomain.com on Google and read the titles and descriptions that come up. Does each one say what that page offers? The fix: a unique title and description per page, one main heading, links between related pages, and schema markup for your business and services. AI tools read the same signals, which I cover in Is your website ready for AI search?

7. It's out of date#

Old prices, a team member who left two years ago, a copyright year from 2021, a booking link that goes nowhere. Each one makes a visitor wonder whether you're still in business.

Check it: read your site as if you were a new customer, and click every button and link on your main pages. The fix: an update pass now, then a monthly check so it doesn't drift again.

What to fix first#

If you found more than one sign, fix them in this order. Each step protects the value of the next one.

  1. 01

    Forms and booking

    Make sure every enquiry arrives. Nothing else matters if leads go nowhere.

  2. 02

    Tracking

    Count each kind of lead, so you can see which pages and ads bring work.

  3. 03

    Calls to action

    Make the next step obvious on every page, especially on phones.

  4. 04

    Speed and mobile

    Trim images, plugins and scripts, and fix layouts that break.

  5. 05

    Search and content

    Unique titles, focused service pages, schema and an update pass.

Most of these are small fixes. Small fixes usually take 1 to 3 days, done on staging first so your live site keeps working while I'm in it.

Questions, answered#

Do I need a new website to fix this?

Usually not. Most lead leaks are fixes to the site you already have. A rebuild makes sense when the platform itself is the problem, and I'll tell you if that's the case.

Which platforms do you work with?

WordPress (Elementor, Gutenberg, WooCommerce), Shopify, GoHighLevel, Squarespace and Wix, plus custom builds in React / Next.js and automations in n8n.

Is my live site safe while you work?

Yes. I work on staging or a duplicate page first, back up with Git, and confirm with you before anything changes on the live site.
